nodes.description: Vezf1-depleted zebrafish show impaired adrenergic augmentation of ventricular systolic function, despite preserved baseline systolic function in the larval measurements. Adult rat cardiomyocyte knockdown reduces cellular shortening. Calcium-transient measurements were unchanged in isolated zebrafish hearts and adult rat cardiomyocytes under the tested conditions; these negative assays do not exclude every excitation-contraction defect. Neither model carries the reported human allele.

nodes.description: In neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocytes, Vezf1 depletion reduces Myh7/beta-MHC and Atp1a2 expression while increasing Acta1/skeletal alpha-actin, lowering the beta-MHC/Ska ratio at RNA and protein levels. Reporter mutagenesis implicates an MCAT element in the Myh7 promoter; Vezf1 co-immunoprecipitates with TEAD-1 from rat left ventricular tissue. The study supports a transcriptional mechanism in experimental systems, not a demonstrated pathway from the reported human allele to DCM.
